name: IVAN SHABANOV
line2: Yerevan, Armenia (GMT+4) · Ready to relocate to Limassol, Cyprus · Remote until relocation, full EU overlap
to: Re: Senior Frontend Developer (Limassol / Paphos, Cyprus)
paragraphs: I am applying for the Senior Frontend Developer position at TradingView. With four years architecting high-performance React and TypeScript applications, I focus on solving the hardest challenges in frontend engineering: data-intensive interfaces, re-render control, complex state management, and real-time streaming data. TradingView sets the global benchmark for financial visualization, and I would love to bring my experience in UI performance and architecture to your product team in Cyprus.

At Alfa-Dengi, I tackled two major frontend architecture challenges. First, our platform experienced severe UI freezing when rendering a 100,000-row lead-scoring dataset with live filters under 9,000 new daily leads. By profiling execution cycles, implementing client-side list virtualization to keep only visible rows in the DOM, and restructuring data paths, I reduced table latency from 8 seconds down to under 1 second. Second, to empower non-technical marketers, I designed and shipped a visual drag-and-drop campaign canvas in React and NestJS. I structured the document model around a normalized Redux Toolkit store with immutable state updates, live graph validation, and per-status frequency limits. The canvas allowed marketers to launch automated multi-step notification campaigns with zero developer involvement, generating about $80K a month.

Across earlier roles at SODA and Appbooster, I concentrated on responsive user journeys and frontend efficiency. At SODA, I raised Lighthouse Performance on high-traffic SPA web applications from 58 to 87 through Core Web Vitals optimization, asset preloading, and layout stability, lifting conversion by roughly 1.5 times. At Appbooster, I built the React user dashboard for a paid task platform, scaling it to 1,000 daily active users in three months with optimistic UI updates and real-time verification queues.

My everyday frontend stack centers on React, TypeScript, Next.js, Redux Toolkit, modern CSS, Vite, WebSocket, and Jest or Vitest. I care deeply about component ergonomics, translating Figma designs into clean design systems, and building fast developer workflows using Claude Code and custom MCP servers.

I am currently based in Yerevan, Armenia (GMT+4) and fully prepared to relocate to Limassol or Paphos for this role, while being ready to begin collaborating remotely under full timezone alignment during the relocation process.

Given TradingView's rich interactive charting, how does your frontend team structure state synchronization between low-level Canvas and WebGL rendering engines and the surrounding React DOM UI layer during rapid market tick updates?
